scenario.prompt_to_agent:
pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports pings to pc2 (200.1.1.2) just time out.
The partner operator reports the reverse direction fails too, but
differently: pings from pc2 toward 195.11.14.x die immediately
with "Destination Net Unreachable" from their own gateway
200.1.1.1. Both sides confirm the eBGP session between router1
and router2 shows Established. Diagnose.

injection.action: remove the network advertisement for pc1's subnet from router1's BGP config

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 BGP configuration (network statement)
Mechanism: router1's `router bgp 1` section no longer contains
  `network 195.11.14.0/24`, so router1 sends router2 an UPDATE
  withdrawing that prefix. The eBGP session itself stays
  Established and router1 still learns 200.1.1.0/24, so the
  FORWARD path pc1 -> router1 -> router2 -> pc2 still delivers.
  The RETURN path is dead: router2 has no route to 195.11.14.0/24,
  so pc2's replies (and pc2-originated pings toward pc1) are
  rejected at router2 with ICMP net-unreachable, sourced from
  200.1.1.1, the router2 interface facing pc2. pc1 therefore sees
  pure timeouts while pc2 sees instant net-unreachable errors.
Localization: router1
Root cause: missing `network 195.11.14.0/24` advertisement in
  router1's BGP configuration
Fix: re-add the network statement on router1 (see [FIX])
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the advertisement on router1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 1" -c "network 195.11.14.0/24"`
router2 re-learns 195.11.14.0/24 and two-way reachability returns.
(A `service frr restart` on router1 also restores it, since /etc/frr/frr.conf
on disk was never modified.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing `network 195.11.14.0/24` advertisement in router1's BGP config
must-identify-mechanism: router2 no longer receives 195.11.14.0/24, so return traffic toward pc1 is unroutable while the eBGP session stays Established
bonus-explains-asymmetry: explains why pc1's pings time out (forward delivered, reply unroutable at router2) while pc2's fail instantly with net-unreachable from 200.1.1.1

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a missing BGP network advertisement on router1. Router2 (AS 2)
correctly includes `network 200.1.1.0/24` under its address-family ipv4 unicast
stanza and successfully advertises that prefix to router1. Router1 (AS 1),
however, has only a bare `neighbor` statement with no `network` command and no
address-family block — it never originates 195.11.14.0/24 into BGP. As a
result, router2's FIB contains no route to 195.11.14.0/24 at all (only its two
directly connected prefixes 193.10.11.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24), and the BGP
summary confirms router2 received exactly 0 prefixes from router1.

This directly explains both symptoms. When pc2 pings 195.11.14.2, its gateway
router2 immediately generates an ICMP Destination Net Unreachable because it has
no matching FIB entry — the packet never leaves router2. When pc1 pings
200.1.1.2, the outbound path works fine (router1 has the BGP-learned route to
200.1.1.0/24 via 193.10.11.2), so packets reach pc2, but pc2's reply is sent
to router2 which again has no route back to 195.11.14.0/24 and silently drops
the return traffic — pc1 sees a clean timeout with no ICMP error.

The eBGP session itself is fully Established (confirmed via `show bgp summary`),
so the control plane peering is healthy; only the prefix origination is missing.

Root cause: router1's BGP configuration lacks a `network 195.11.14.0/24`
statement, so the 195.11.14.0/24 prefix is never advertised to AS 2.

Corrective fix: add the following to router1's FRR configuration:
  router bgp 1
    address-family ipv4 unicast
      network 195.11.14.0/24
    exit-address-family
This will cause router1 to originate 195.11.14.0/24 into eBGP, router2 will
install it in its FIB, and bidirectional reachability will be restored.
